t: In front of you is the Monument, a tall fluted Doric column near the northern end of London Bridge. It stands two hundred and two feet high, and it stands two hundred and two feet from Pudding Lane, where the Great Fire started on the second of September, 1666. It was built between 1671 and 1677 on the site of St Margaret's, the first church the fire destroyed. Christopher Wren and Robert Hooke designed it. Wren was given the job of rebuilding fifty-two City churches, while Hooke surveyed more than half the property lines as the city was rebuilt. Caius Gabriel Cibber made it too.
